Lists all users in a Slack team.
Gets the access logs for the current team.

assumptions: People are read from the workspace-wide user listing (users.list), which includes deactivated people (they come back marked deleted). Nothing about the signed-in caller is used to build the list.
There is no last-activity or last-login timestamp on a Slack user record, so usage is taken from the workspace access log (team.accessLogs), which reports login activity per user.

The access-log endpoint is an admin endpoint; Slack documents admin-scope endpoints as needing an admin token and generally a paid plan. The provided documentation does not name a plan, so no plan requirement is set and the usage step may fail on free workspaces.
The access log only offers a 'before' cut-off, not a start of window, so no usage window is configured; the connector reads the log page by page as the endpoint returns it.

Slack does not offer a client-credentials (machine-to-machine) flow. The authorization-code install flow with the issued bot/user token is the only server-side option in the documentation, and a long-lived bot token is the more durable of the two token types.

The documentation shows the token passed both as a query parameter and as a 'token' header; both are offered as connection options. Slack's preferred bearer-header style is not shown explicitly in the source, so it is not offered.
Role is derived only from the is_admin flag (admin vs member). Owner, primary owner and other workspace roles are not distinguished.
User type is derived only from the is_bot flag: Slack guests (is_restricted / is_ultra_restricted) and external members will appear as member, and bot or app users as service.
Slack user records carry no account creation timestamp, so createdAt is left empty, and lastActiveAt is left empty because activity is reported through the access log instead.
The documentation does not state a maximum page size, so 200 users per request and 100 access-log entries per request were chosen as sensible values.

Slack answers with HTTP 200 and an 'ok' flag; the source does not show the name of the error message field or any error codes, so only the success flag is configured and no rate-limit or auth codes are listed.
No rate limits or rate-limit headers are stated in the source, so all rate-limit settings are left empty.
No tenant-specific host or extra header is needed: every workspace uses the same API root and the token identifies the workspace.
